doc.title: Bobby Johnson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998

title: Megaphones and visiting New Orleans bands
summary: Before microphones singers used megaphones, and visiting bands let the local kid play.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: Yes, I would love to know about getting a visit — you said King Oliver presented your—

Okay, well like I said, during those days, when the bands would come from New Orleans, like Papa Celestin, Don Albert, King Oliver, and other bands from Chicago, see bands that was based in Chicago, they all came from New Orleans, see? But that was their home town. And people would say, “Hey, let the kid play something — why don’t you let the kid play something?” And even during those days you sang, and this was before microphones or anything, this was during the days when we used to sing Rudy Vallee with a megaphone you know. And we’d say, “Pass the mege.”
